text:
maria: Quick check — need to lock the seq-dist + prefill-dominant benchmark protocol before the kernel swap tomorrow morning. Proposed: three workloads (short-only 8-64, mid 64-512, prefill-heavy: prefill 2048 then generate 512). Use both synthetic and replay harness for each.
kevin: +1. Also: run cold vs warm KV cache toggles (cold = empty KV, warm = primed with prefix set).
ashwin: +1 from me too (can't make meeting). Important: compare kernel selection paths — fused-attn vs matmul fallback, and also quantized kernel where available. Record kernel choice per request.
sara: FYI perfbot alerted about a p99 regression on fused-v2 yesterday; we need strict apples-to-apples: same seqlen distribution, batching policy, and same routing rules.
perfbot: profiling snapshot (sample): CPU time distribution during prefill-heavy run: memcpy 42.3%, attention-kernel 28.7%, kernel-dispatch 9.5%, other 19.5%. Heap high-water ~3.1GB.
bench-runner: I'll scaffold runs. Suggested harness command: `./harness/run_bench --profile=cpu --scenario=prefill-heavy --replay=synthetic --batch-policy=continuous --batch-sizes=1,4,8 --kernels=fused,matmul,quant`.
maria: Perfect. Also add an explicit KV eviction test: repeated long-prefill requests to force KV fragmentation and observe fallback to matmul.
kevin: Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec steady-state, kernel-select counts, memcpy rate, GPU occupancy, memory high-water, and cost-per-token estimate.
ashwin: For apples-to-apples, use the same seqlen histogram file across both synthetic and replay runs (I can export from prod anonymized buckets). Use the `--seqlen-hist=seqlen_v2.json` flag.
sara: Regression gate: fail if p99 increases >5% OR throughput drops >10% OR kernel-fallback rate doubles. Mark failures as blocker for kernel swap.
bench-runner: I'll run full matrix overnight (3 workloads x 3 batch sizes x 3 kernels x cold/warm = 54 runs). Will push results to the perf dashboard under `prefill-protocol/1823456789`.
maria: For reproducibility include raw harness config in artifacts and `perf trace` output (top 10 symbols). Small sample config to attach: ```
{
  "scenario":"prefill-heavy",
  "replay":"synthetic",
  "batch_policy":"continuous",
  "batch_sizes":[1,4,8],
  "kernels":["fused","matmul","quant"],
  "kv_cache":"warm",
  "seqlen_hist":"seqlen_v2.json"
}
```
kevin: One more: capture memory allocator stats and slab fragmentation (jemalloc stats). Prefill-dominant runs often surface allocator churn that looks like kernel perf problems.
ashwin: Agree. We'll include `jemalloc.stats` and `nvprof` flame samples for a subset of runs.
sara: If bench-runner sees the same regression as perfbot, next step is a narrow bisection: revert last fused-v2 change on staging and rerun the single-workload test.
bench-runner: Ack. I'll start with synthetic runs tonight, then replay with anonymized customer logs tomorrow. Will post short summary + artifacts link here when done. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks — sync at 10am if regressions show up. If everything looks green we'll proceed with kernel swap at 15:00. :shipit:
